title: IPC initialization cannot be retried after initializer failure
reasoning: initializeMainProcessIpcOnce flips mainProcessIpcHandlersInitialized to true before calling initializer. If initializer throws partway through registration, the runtime is left marked initialized and every later call returns false, preventing recovery or a clean retry of missing handlers in the same process.
recommendation: Set the initialized flag only after initializer completes successfully, or catch errors, reset the flag, and rethrow so callers can retry or fail clearly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and there is no evidence of a test covering a throwing initializer path.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test that passes an initializer which throws, verifies a second call attempts initialization again, then verifies a successful initializer prevents further retries.
minimumFixScope: Change initializeMainProcessIpcOnce error handling and add a focused test for thrown and successful initializer cases.
